chunks: And let those who do not find the means for marriage abstain (from unlawful sexual relations) until God enriches them from His grace.
And those from your slaves who seek a written deed of manumission, give them such a deed if you know any good in them, and give them out of the wealth of God which He has given you.
And do not force your maidservants to prostitution if they wish to remain chaste, in order to acquire the goods of this world.
And if someone forces them, then surely God, after their forced helplessness, is Forgiving, Merciful.
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic rulings on manumitting slaves and forcing maidservants into prostitution?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to establish the social welfare duty of the community, particularly the Imam or ruler, to provide for those unable to marry. It highlights the concept of 'kitabah' (deed of manumission) as a transitional mechanism for slaves, emphasizing that their earnings and manumission funds are ultimately derived from God's provision. The prohibition against forcing chaste maidservants into prostitution underscores the preservation of their moral integrity, with divine mercy extended even if they are compelled.
